## Rule

Generator source read 2026-06-09: `external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_29623171.py`.

Task059 is a fixed 11x11 Hollywood-squares board. Color 5 is always the divider
at rows `3,7` and cols `3,7`, making nine 3x3 compartments. The generator places
one nonzero non-5 object color in the compartments, with each compartment holding
0..max_pixels sampled cells. Output preserves the color-5 divider grid, clears
all non-winning compartments to background, and fills every compartment whose
object-cell count equals the maximum count. Ties are real and all tied
compartments are filled.

## Algorithm sketch

Reference recipe: `Research_Archive/notes/recipe-task059-grid-max-count-fill.md`.

Current staged graph (`task059_einsum_basis5_cost861`) uses a 5-row basis for
the active 11x11 board: group rows/cols are `[0:3]`, divider `3`, `[4:7]`,
divider `7`, `[8:11]`. One F32 Einsum counts object occupancy over the 5x5 group
grid, `ReduceMax+Equal` marks every max-count compartment, and one F16 Einsum
renders the full `[1,10,30,30]` one-hot output directly from:

```python
counts = einsum(input, object_channel_mask, basis5_count, basis5_count)
selected = counts == counts.max()
present_color = input.max(axis=(2, 3))
output = einsum([background_plane, divider_lines, selected_blocks],
                [background_channel, divider_channel, object_channel],
                basis5, basis5)
```

This avoids the live graph's 11x11 crop, ten channel slices, ConvTranspose fill
mask, and 10-channel 11x11 concat.
